listening_questions: Does B sound more like one guitarist striking a three-note power-chord shape rather than three perfectly simultaneous MIDI notes?
Does the approximately 37 ms total strum spread remain tight enough for Rock rather than sounding arpeggiated?
Does alternating low-to-high/high-to-low direction feel natural or draw attention to itself?
Does preserving the original absolute note-off prevent the strum from adding extra sustain or smear?
rejection_conditions: B sounds flammy, rolled, arpeggiated, or rhythmically late.
Alternating direction sounds mechanical or patterned.
B weakens the attack or punch compared with A.
The onset spread becomes more noticeable than the chord itself.
approval_condition: B must sound more guitar-like than A without losing Rock attack tightness.
